guarantees.claim: absorbed_o is a single-cycle pulse: when mubi4_test_true_strict(absorbed_o) is true, the next cycle mubi4_test_false_strict(absorbed_o) is true.
keccak_run_o is a single-cycle pulse: when high, the next cycle it is low.

assumptions.claim: start_i is a single-cycle pulse: after rising, it must fall in the next cycle.
assumptions.risk: If start_i stays high for multiple cycles, the start condition may be misinterpreted, leading to double-triggering or missed state transitions.

assumptions.claim: process_i is a single-cycle pulse: after rising, it must fall in the next cycle.
assumptions.risk: If process_i stays high for multiple cycles, the module may process data incorrectly or advance its state machine unexpectedly.

assumptions.claim: done_i is a single-cycle pulse: mubi4_test_true_strict(done_i) implies mubi4_test_false_strict(done_i) in the next cycle.
assumptions.risk: If done_i is not cleanly pulsed, the module may detect a false or repeated done condition, potentially causing illegal state transitions or data corruption.

assumptions.claim: At most one of {start_i, process_i, mubi4_test_true_loose(done_i)} is high at any time (one-hot0).
assumptions.risk: If multiple control inputs are active simultaneously, the state machine may enter an ambiguous or illegal state, causing protocol violation or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: No formal assumption enforces the intended sequence start_i → process_i → absorbed_o → done_i. The commented-out SVA rule (line 769) indicates the designer intended this ordering but could not easily express it. The presented assumptions only enforce pulse shape and mutual exclusion, leaving open the possibility of out-of-order control pulses.
uncertain_points.cond: When the environment drives the interface
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-order pulses may cause the SHA3 padding process to absorb data incorrectly or miss proper completion sequencing.
